This game has very limited control options and is much more of an arcade-style game than I was expecting. All cars are equipped with a 5 speed automatic transmission and auto-reverse is locked on like it is a need for speed game. There is no way to disable auto reverse or shift gears manually. The steering feels sloppy even on cars like the K1500 which should feel pretty tight. Upgrades necessary to proceed are locked behind a leveling system which takes forever to grind. The first map, Michigan, is completely saturated with mud and good mud tires are locked behind 5 or 6 levels. The other options are not much better, because it is either mud or ice, and ice tires are locked behind even more levels.

All of these problems really suck even more because the terrain deformation is some of the most realistic there is, but enjoyment is hampered by the arcadey vehicles that all feel the same and the massive grind to unlock bare minimum equipment. If you are looking for a game to drive trucks around in then BeamNG.drive is the better game and if you are looking for a game to put trucks to work then the Farm Simulator series is better. I was heavily disappointed in this game after I had heard so many people talk about it.

SnowRunner is a surprisingly deep and satisfying vehicle simulation. The physics feel incredibly realistic, especially when navigating mud, rivers, snow, and steep inclines. Every vehicle handles differently, and learning how to manage weight, traction, and load feels rewarding. The variety of trucks, terrain, and missions makes exploration engaging, and the feeling of finally getting a stuck truck out of a swamp is oddly satisfying.

The game is challenging and sometimes frustrating. Progress can be slow, and some missions feel repetitive or tedious. The maps are large, but travel can be slow if your vehicle is underpowered. The controls and camera can occasionally be awkward, and it can take time to master the different vehicles.

Overall, SnowRunner is not about speed or flashy action. It is about patience, strategy, and realistic off-road challenges. For anyone who loves vehicle simulations or open-world problem-solving, it is extremely rewarding. Even as someone who is not a car enthusiast, I found myself hooked on testing vehicles and mastering tricky terrain.

⭐ 8 out of 10

This is one of my top 3 video games all time. I have over 500 hours on PS4/PS5. The problem with this game is that most people will never even give it a chance because it is a "trucking game". However, it is a gamer's game. The trucks are characters, and we all have our favorites. The challenge is there. The puzzle solving and critical thinking are there. Progression is rewarding. I'm convinced anyone who enjoys the challenge and earned progression of classic video games will love this game. You have to prepare, plan and execute to be successful. Make a mistake?...recover your truck and cargo from the bottom of a mountain. This is a RESILIENCY SIMULATOR, and I love it. 

The Dev Team has been awesome, constantly updating the game and adding new content. I don't even warn my wife I'm buying the DLCs anymore. She just knows its going to happen.

Overall this is a very relaxing game once you get comfortable with how the game works and you get your feet wet. After unlocking more later game areas you can unlock some really powerful and really, really cool trucks that are major upgrades from the starting ones. You get a lot of choices for what trucks you can use to complete tasks, there is no specific or required order to beat the game. You just pick what you are comfortable with and what you find to be fun. Excellent game design overall! Another great benefit to the game is you CAN buy DLC packs but it is never required. The trucks you unlock over time are enough to carry you through the entire game.

Seems like anymore they spend more money on garbage marketing than actually making the game better.

As for this game, visually it looks great, but has one of the worst "simulation" engines I've had the displeasure of experiencing. From how it looks to me, there's more realism in how the mud visually gets deformed by driving through it, but as for a realistic simulation of the trucks themselves: JUNK.

A very obvious example that comes up quite often, is how in a 4-wheel scout truck with giant wheels, being maybe a few INCHES deep in mud, not being held by anything, will be in 4th gear, all 4 tires spinning very fast, and yet I'll be moving 1.5 MPH. It's garbage. You'll also get damaged by going too fast on clear, straight, paved roads. Nearly every truck becomes unstable over 20 MPH on paved "highways" as well.

I keep coming back to this, as I REALLY want to enjoy this game, but I end up quitting every time because of how simply annoying and frustrating it is to play. If it was more "realistic" but made sense, I would probably love this, but instead it's a poor example of a "simulation" game.
